subject: System Design
title: Idempotency
description: A micro-lesson that makes Idempotency usable.

hook.text: A payment request times out. Did it go through? You retry. Now the customer might be charged twice.

buildup.text: An idempotent operation produces the same result no matter how many times it's executed.

discovery.text: Assigning an idempotency key to each request lets the server detect retries and return the cached result.

twist.text: Not all operations are naturally idempotent. 'Add $100' is not idempotent. 'Set balance to $500' is.

climax.text: In distributed systems where retries are inevitable, idempotency is the only safe way to handle them.

punchline.text: Make every operation safe to retry — always.

quiz.question: What makes an operation idempotent?
options: It produces the same result no matter how many times it runs
